name: fit-visualizer
description: FIT file viewer and analyzer: charts, map, climb/descent segments, heart-rate zones, ride history and AI-assisted training analysis

fitVisualizer.maxHeartRate.description: Legacy fallback maximum heart rate. Dated profiles entered in the activity view take precedence.

fitVisualizer.logLlmRequests.description: Write each Copilot prompt and response to .fit-visualizer/logs next to the database.

fitVisualizer.llmLogRetentionDays.description: Delete Copilot request logs older than this many days. Set to 0 to keep them forever.

fitVisualizer.llmChatLogRetentionDays.description: Delete Copilot chat and comparison logs older than this many days. Conversations are kept longer than one-off analysis logs. Set to 0 to keep them forever.

fitVisualizer.lmVendor.description: VS Code language-model vendor ID used for activity analysis and chat.

fitVisualizer.preferCheapAnalysisModel.description: For one-off activity analysis (not chat), use the cheapest available Copilot model by published per-token price instead of whichever model Copilot lists first. Run FIT: Update Model Prices to refresh the local price table from GitHub. Unknown models fall back to an Auto model family, then to a model-name heuristic. Turn off to use the default model. None of this is officially guaranteed by the VS Code API.

fitVisualizer.analysisModelId.description: Pin one-off activity analysis to a specific language-model id (overrides the cheapest-model selection). Useful for reproducing prompt experiments; the log records which model answered.

fitVisualizer.comparisonModelId.description: Pin AI comparisons to a specific language-model id (overrides the default middle-tier selection). Leave empty to use the automatic default. The dropdown next to the Compare button overrides it for one comparison.

fitVisualizer.chatModelId.description: Pin follow-up chat to a specific language-model id (overrides the default middle-tier selection). Leave empty to use the automatic default. The dropdown under the chat input overrides it for one reply.

fitVisualizer.cheapModelMarkers.description: Model name substrings (case-insensitive) used to pick a cheaper model when fitVisualizer.preferCheapAnalysisModel is enabled and none of the available models is in the current local price table.

fitVisualizer.powerModel.dragArea.description: Effective frontal area CdA in m² used when power is estimated from motion. Roughly 0.25 tucked on a time-trial bike, 0.32 on the hoods, 0.40 or more sitting upright.

fitVisualizer.powerModel.rollingResistan.description: Rolling resistance coefficient Crr used when power is estimated from motion. Roughly 0.004 for road tyres on asphalt, higher for wider or knobbly tyres.

fitVisualizer.segmentation.gradeThreshol.description: Grade in percent that separates climbs and descents from flat terrain.

fitVisualizer.segmentation.gradeHysteres.description: Extra grade margin required to switch terrain type, preventing flapping around the threshold.

fitVisualizer.segmentation.minSegmentSec.description: Shorter segments are merged into a neighbour.

fitVisualizer.segmentation.technicalGrad.description: Descent grade below which an erratic speed trace marks the segment as technical (no effort estimate).

fitVisualizer.segmentation.effortMinSegm.description: Shortest stretch of steady effort that becomes a segment of its own. Segments follow heart rate and power; the terrain only names them.

fitVisualizer.segmentation.effortHrStepB.description: Heart-rate difference (bpm) that counts as a different level of effort when it lasts for the minimum segment length. Lower values give more segments.

fitVisualizer.segmentation.effortPowerSt.description: Power difference (W, measured or estimated) that counts as a different level of effort. Lower values give more segments.

fitVisualizer.segmentation.stopSpeedKmh.description: Speed at or below which a record counts as stopped.

fitVisualizer.segmentation.stopMinSecond.description: Minimum duration of a stop, and the recording gap that counts as an auto-paused stop.

fitVisualizer.segmentation.gpsTrustMinKm.description: Minimum continuous distance before a GPS window can confirm the recorded speed.

enumDescriptions: Load OpenStreetMap tiles over the network (the tile server sees which map area you view).
Draw the route on a plain background with no network requests.
fitVisualizer.map.tiles.description: Map tile source. "none" keeps the map fully offline: the route is drawn without a background map and no tile requests are made.
